findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - an existing client upgrades and syncs while retaining its app-owned permissions.
The `earlier adopted` case initializes a fresh app using the current Forge, then compares its files with current templates. `_fresh_client` creates an empty repository and invokes the current `forge init` (tests/test_setup.py:197–209). This neither exercises an earlier-adopted app nor detects sync overwriting customized permissions with template defaults. Use an earlier-adopted fixture and compare its app files before and after sync.
findings.title: Gate: earlier-adopted permissions survive sync

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - shipping the new Show deleted and Restore interfaces.
The implementation commit explicitly records that the impeccable and emil-design-eng pass was not run. The existing CHECKS.md covers design artboards and their images (docs/design/FORGE-FEATURE-1/CHECKS.md:3–4), rather than the implemented screens. The required audit and polish of the rendered permissions and restore states remains unfinished; the browser flows and axe checks do not complete that inspection.
findings.title: Gate: UI check

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2 (floor: module tables)
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - loading projects with the deleting account's email.
This new scalar subquery reads `core.account` directly from the projects module, although auth owns that table (apps/api/app/auth/models.py:10–16 in the Python starter). The TypeScript counterpart also adds a direct `deletedByAccount` lookup in libs/projects/server/src/projects.service.ts:13. These additions violate the requirement that another module's tables be reached through its public service. Obtain the deleting account's email through auth's public boundary in both starters.
findings.title: Module tables: projects query the deleting account directly
